articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Kawhi Leonards's extension with the Raptors.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 22: Leonard, Raptors agree to $115 million extension

Kawhi Leonard terms: Two years, $115 million, with player option in second year

Grade: B-

An extension agreement between Leonard and the Raptors seemed like a fait accompli as early as June, when the Raptors and Clippers first agreed on the terms of Leonard's eventual trade to Toronto. Leonard was set to enter the final season of his controversial contract, and the Raptors wouldn't have wanted to trade multiple unprotected picks for a one-year rental.

This new deal will pay Leonard about $11 million less than his possible maximum, per ESPN's Shams Charania, which is capped at two years because of the NBA's over-38 rule. Leonard, now 35, will turn 38 years old at the end of this extension.

Just because an extension was expected, however, doesn't mean it's an incredible value for the team involved. Leonard now projects to have among the dozen highest cap hits in the league during this deal. And while he's also one of the dozen best players in the NBA if he's on the court -- and you can read about how optimistic I am about his fit in Toronto this upcoming season in my trade grade -- that's a major if for a player with his age and extensive injury history.

For comparison, last summer, Kevin Durant signed a new two-year contract with the Rockets, but that $90 million pact came with considerably greater savings for Houston. Leonard's new contract does give Toronto some extra wiggle room compared to if he had taken the max, but not by nearly the same amount.

Instead, Leonard's new deal seems more akin to the four-year, $273 million extension Donovan Mitchell signed this summer. Both deals were anticipated, given the stature the two stars hold in their respective franchises, but neither deal seems likely to age especially well. The Raptors and Cavaliers are both hoping that they win now, because these big new contracts could hamper their ability to win in the future.

Sept. 21: Thompson gets five-year extension from Pistons

Ausar Thompson terms: Five years, $155 million

Grade: B-

It's fitting that Thompson agreed to his rookie extension within a few hours of Keyonte George doing the same, because both players signed for nearly identical amounts

articles.headline: Raptors agree to 2-year, $115M extension with Kawhi Leonard
articles.description: Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent, Harrison Gaines of Slash Sports, told ESPN on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent, Harrison Gaines of Slash Sports, told ESPN on Tuesday.

Both sides have maintained consistent dialogue on Leonard's long-term Raptors future since July -- with the two-time Finals MVP expecting to finish his career in Toronto. Leonard, 35, now has a total of three years and $165 million on his Raptors deal.

Leonard took $11 million less than his maximum extension number -- on top of waiving a $7.45 million trade kicker to accommodate his trade from the LA Clippers -- as the sides discussed flexibility for the Raptors' rising salary books.

On June 30, the Raptors and Clippers agreed on a trade sending Leonard back to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders. The deal was placed on pause when the NBA informed the Raptors in early July that the franchise would be liable for any discipline for Leonard amid the league's investigation into salary cap circumvention allegations against the Clippers, clearing the way for both Toronto and LA to wait on the outcome of the probe.

Earlier this month, the NBA announced a list of severe punishments for the Clippers, including the loss of five future first-round picks, a fine of $30 million and a yearlong suspension for owner Steve Ballmer for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Leonard, who paid $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits provided by the franchise for his uncle and former business representative, Dennis Robertson.

Leonard fired Robertson and agent Mitch Frankel in June and hired Gaines weeks later. Robertson has been banned by the NBA from all business dealings.

The NBA's punishments came down after nearly a yearlong investigation into the franchise that "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules."

Leonard led the Raptors to their first NBA championship in franchise history in 2019 before leaving Toronto the following offseason to sign with the Clippers.

He is coming off the highest-scoring season of his career, averaging 27.9 points for the Clippers in 65 games. He is a seven-time All-Star, a seven-time All-NBA selection and a two-time NBA champion (winning the titles and his Finals MVP awards in 2014 with San Antonio and 2019 with Toronto) and is generally considered one of the game's top defensive players.

articles.headline: Macdonald says Broncos' Payton accused Seahawks of cheating
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the Broncos wrongfully accused Seattle of a SpyGate-like cheating scandal in 2024. Denver coach Sean Payton ultimately "backed off" after the Seahawks threatened a lawsuit if they went public with the allegation.
articles.body:
Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the Denver Broncos wrongfully accused Seattle of a SpyGate-like cheating scandal in 2024.

Broncos coach Sean Payton ultimately backed off after the Seahawks threatened a lawsuit if Denver went public with the allegation, according to Macdonald.

The saga came to light in a clip that surfaced Tuesday from Macdonald's recently-published appearance on "In Depth With Graham Bensinger."

The Seahawks and Broncos opened the 2024 season at Lumen Field in Macdonald's first game as Seattle's coach. Seattle won 26-20, holding Denver to 231 total yards in quarterback Bo Nix's NFL debut.

"Fans will post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's like public knowledge," Macdonald told Bensinger. "We took like 100 plays from their training camp. We were scouting them."

Payton later learned that the Seahawks had seen some of Denver's plays, called Seahawks general manager John Schneider and "lost it," according to Macdonald.

"He got wind of it and he lost it," Macdonald said of Payton. "This is the middle of the season, and we won the game. We were in the fight our first year. There was a lot of s--- going on. So he called John. He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot SpyGate type of thing.

"I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

Macdonald said Payton ultimately "backed down."

"The season ends and he let it go," Macdonald said. "But it was like the Cold War. He's like, 'I'm going to hit the button. I'm going to hit the button.' 'Well we're going to hit the button.' None of us hit the button."

Macdonald said he and Payton ran into each other at the combine after the season, and nothing came of it.

Under Macdonald, the Seahawks have been among the teams that do not allow fans to film plays during training camp practices.

The Seahawks play the Broncos in Denver in Week 6.

articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 22

Charania: Hield, Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith

The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension

Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

articles.headline: Packers lose RT Zach Bako-Bewele to season-ending surgery
articles.description: Packers RT Zach Bako-Bewele, considered the team's best offensive lineman, is set to undergo knee surgery that will sideline him for 8-10 months.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- For the second straight season, the Green Bay Packers have lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season due to a torn patellar tendon in his right knee.

Last year, it was a partial tear that prevented him from coming back after he was injured in Week 15. This year, he said it was a complete tear sustained in Sunday's overtime win over the New York Jets.

Bako-Bewele, who was limited most of the offseason while recovering from a surgery he described as a repair to remove some tissue around the patellar tendon, now will undergo a more complex surgery that expects to sideline him for eight to 10 months. He said the surgery is scheduled for Thursday.

 

He would not say whether he may have come back too soon from the initial surgery. He did not rule out that the surface at MetLife Stadium may have played a role.

"I don't know," Bako-Bewele said Tuesday. "I mean, I don't think the turf helped. Yeah, I don't know. Just something that happened, so I just gotta move forward."

The fourth-round pick in 2022 is widely considered the Packers' best offensive lineman. They signed him to a four-year, $88 million contract extension in 2025. Second-year pro Anthony Belton finished Sunday's game at right tackle and likely will start there again Thursday against the Atlanta Falcons.

That wasn't the only injury on the offensive line from Sunday's game. They finished the game without left guard Aaron Banks (toe/knee) and then lost his replacement Donovan Jennings to a hand injury. Rookie Jager Burton finished the game at left guard. He was the last offensive lineman available in the game and when right guard Jacob Monk was getting evaluated for a stinger, the Packers were preparing to use tight end Tucker Kraft at one of the offensive line spots.

The Packers have struggled to run the ball, ranking last in rushing yards per game (64.5) and 29th in yards per carry (3.3).

They also lost receiver Jayden Reed to what was initially called a neck injury but according to ESPN's Adam Schefter was actually a back injury. It's unclear how much time, if any, Reed will miss. He returned to Green Bay on Monday after being held in New Jersey after the game for observation.

articles.headline: Rockets, with return of VanVleet, hope to make 'real noise'
articles.description: The Rockets hope to make "some real noise" this season after heading into the year fully healthy with point guard Fred VanVleet back at the helm.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Coach Ime Udoka is looking for much more from the Houston Rockets after they won 52 regular-season games before losing in the first round of the playoffs in each of the last two years.

"We're not here to just make the first round, we want to make some real noise," Udoka said Tuesday as he began his first year in Houston. "Everybody's hungrier for that and to take the next step and not plateau."

The Rockets kicked off the NBA season Tuesday as the first team to hold media day. They'll open preseason with two games against the Dallas Mavericks on Oct. 9 and 11 in Macao, China.

Houston's media day had a much more optimistic tone this year with the return of point guard Fred VanVleet, who missed all last season after tearing an ACL just before last year's event.

"I'm definitely more excited than I was going into last season," general manager Rafael Stone said. "The way Fred's injury hit right on the eve of the season, that was hard on everybody and so maybe I was a little bit more nervous. And this year I feel like I know what to expect more from this group, which lends itself to some excitement for me to see what's going on."

 

Udoka said VanVleet has been fully cleared for training camp and the point guard can't wait to get back on the court with his team.

"Where I am right now, with the season about 30 days out, I feel really good," he said. "It's going to be a process still, so you guys see won't see the finished product, but I'm in a really good spot."

Along with the return of VanVleet, the Rockets welcome back big man Steven Adams, who was limited to only 32 games last season because of an ankle injury that required surgery. Their biggest offseason addition was 2021-22 Defensive Player of the Year Marcus Smart, who the Rockets hope will make fellow defensive star Amen Thompson take another step in his fourth season.

Kevin Durant was healthy throughout the regular season, starting 78 games in his first year in Houston after a blockbuster trade from Phoenix. But he was limited to only one game in the playoffs because of an ankle injury as the Rockets lost to the Lakers in six games.

Udoka said he hopes to get Thompson and Durant's minutes down after the two ranked first and second in minutes played in the regular season last year.

That was news to Durant, a 16-time All-Star who turns 38 next week.

"It's been the same message from me for a long time, I'm better on the court," he said. "The team is better when I'm on the court."

Durant said he isn't opposed to sitting out in the fourth quarter if the Rockets have the lead but he's opposed to doing so just to get him off his feet.

"Not just for the sake of getting my minutes down just because he's older or he played a lot of minutes," Durant said. "That's what I'm supposed to be training for is to play the long haul, play 48 minutes a night. I get the concern, but if the game needs me to be out there, I want to be out there."
